meaning: The script scores one k-medoids partition of beats against three held-out labels (model, run, phase) and treats those three ARI values as mutually exclusive at a given k. That framing is what turns the numbers into a test of what the beat descriptors encode rather than a restatement.

could_move.what: The exclusivity claim holds only if the three labels are not themselves correlated in the pooled sample; the sample mixes models with a parameter grid, so model and run labels can be partly nested.
Which models enter the pooled sample sets the model-label contrast. The reach resolves only m4, while decks pair m4 against m1, m3 and m5.
Phase labels come from the compression protocol, so beats-per-phase balance differs across protocol decks and can shift ARI vs phase.
Sweep decks contribute many run labels at fixed model, inflating the number of run classes relative to model classes.
Both representations are reported, so the headline ARI depends on which one is quoted in the CIS report figures.

expectation: Unknown. It depends on label balance in the pooled beat set, which is not visible here. If run labels greatly outnumber model labels, ARI vs run is likely depressed at small k, which would make the model signal look stronger than it is.

check.why: Reruns the scoring on modelplots output already written by the sweep, with no re-fit, so the label counts and the three ARI values can be read directly. The reach found no entry points, so if this flag does not exist the command fails fast and tells us how the script is meant to be invoked.
